newsitem.title: USA: Atmos Energy sees impact next year.
newsitem.headline: Atmos Energy sees impact next year.

text.p: Atmos Energy Corp Wednesday reported lower second quarter, ended March 31, earnings citing warm weather and said the impact of current efforts will be seen in 1998 and beyond.
Second quarter earnings per share dropped to $0.90 after a $0.17 charge for payments to two former executives. This compares to $1.15 pe share a year earlier.

Winter heating sales for the quarter were affected by weather that was 6 percent warmer than normal, and 7 percent warmer than last year's second quarter. The effect of the weather was partially offset by rate increases.

"Revenues were 5 percent higher in 1997's second quarter due to increased gas costs. Expenses for the quarter also increased over the same period in 1996. Although we served more customers and benefited from rate increases, our earnings were affected by the warmer winter weather and by one-time administrative and general expenses," said Chief Executive Robert W. Best, who joined the company March 7 from Consolidated Natural Gas Co.
The company also noted Larry J. Dagley joined Atmos on May 1 as chief financial officer. He previously was chief financial officer for Pacific Enterprises.

Best said Atmos is proceeding with obtaining regulatory approval in Illinois for its merger with United Cities Gas Co. Necessary approvals have been obtained in nine other states. The company has extended its merger agreement until August 31, but expects to close the merger earlier.

During the quarter Atmos announced a 12-month plan to enhance customer service and operating efficiency by implementing a central customer support call center, establishing a network of payment centers at convenience stores offering extended hours for customers and closing its business offices to walk-in traffic. The company expects a net reduction of 240 jobs as a result of the changes.
"For 1998 and beyond, we expect to begin to see the impact of the important moves we are making in 1997 with the call center and the United Cities merger," Best said.
He said the company will seek to grow by both acquisitions and through internal growth.

Noting the board had declared an unchanged quarterly dividend of $0.25 per share, Atmos noted it has agreed to increase the annual dividend to not less than $1.02 at the first board meeting following the completion of the United Cities merger. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
